title: Module equivalence and internal Hom for the lifted small site
statement: Let C be a category with objects in universe u+1 and morphisms in universe u, let J be a Grothendieck topology [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let R be a sheaf of commutative rings in universe u+1. Give AsSmall(C) the topology induced by its inverse lift and restrict R to a ring sheaf Rsmall. Restriction along the forward lift gives an additive equivalence Q from Rsmall-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] to R-module sheaves. For every M,N there is a canonical isomorphism Q(Hom_Rsmall(M,N)) ≅ Hom_R(QM,QN) [def-pur-sheaf-hom], natural for precomposition and postcomposition. On a slice W→U it retains the component of the map on the lifted slice.

source.place: Internal-Hom comparison and naturality of evaluation paragraph; ordinary small-site restriction and Frobenius translation.

proof.text: Transport the topology by AsSmall.down. Both directions are continuous. The pushforwardPushforwardEquivalence with identity coefficient maps gives Q and its inverse; the unit and counit equations reduce to restriction along identity arrows. Addition of maps is pointwise.

At each U, send a map over its lifted slice to the same components at lifts of W→U. Conversely use the underlying arrows. Naturality follows from the same commuting triangles. Both composites are identity on each module section; scalar multiplication is the same restricted coefficient action.

These linear slice isomorphisms commute with every restriction, so isoMk makes a sheaf isomorphism. Precomposition and postcomposition are componentwise composition, so the two-variable naturality equation is reflexivity on every slice and section.
